boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Louisville rituals, symbols, songs, and recurring recognitions.

cards.title: Avoid the Cardinal Bird Sidewalk Emblem
cards.subtitle: Belknap Campus tradition
cards.notes: Notice the Cardinal Bird emblem as you cross campus, then take the long way around it if you want to follow the alumni-documented bad-luck ritual.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition centers on not stepping on the Cardinal Bird set into a sidewalk.
cards.evidence_claim: UofL's alumni office lists never stepping on the Cardinal Bird as a UofL tradition and calls it bad luck.
cards.access_notes: Observe the emblem and use normal pedestrian routes; do not obstruct walkways.

cards.title: Put Your L's Up With Your Right Hand
cards.subtitle: Cardinal pride gesture
cards.notes: Use the right hand when joining an L's Up photo or cheer; the university's alumni tradition page specifically distinguishes it from the left-hand version.
cards.short_summary: The right-handed L's Up gesture is a documented Cardinal sign of pride.
cards.evidence_claim: UofL's alumni office identifies the U-and-L American Sign Language combination as a Cardinal symbol and says to throw it with the right hand.
cards.access_notes: Appropriate for campus events and photos.

cards.title: Watch for the Albino Squirrels
cards.subtitle: Belknap Campus good-luck lore
cards.notes: Keep an eye out for the campus's white squirrels while walking between classes; the lore attaches good fortune to a sighting, not a guarantee.
cards.short_summary: Spotting an albino squirrel is tied to UofL good-luck folklore.
cards.evidence_claim: UofL's alumni office says albino-squirrel sightings are associated with good luck, including lore about tuition or exams.
cards.access_notes: View wildlife from a respectful distance; do not feed or approach animals.

cards.title: Take a Photo With The Thinker
cards.subtitle: In front of Grawemeyer Hall
cards.notes: Bring a friend and make a quick photo stop with Rodin's The Thinker in front of Grawemeyer Hall, following the alumni-documented campus custom.
cards.short_summary: Photos with UofL's Rodin cast are an alumni-recognized campus tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UofL's alumni office lists having a picture taken with The Thinker in front of Grawemeyer Hall as a UofL tradition.
cards.access_notes: View the outdoor sculpture from public campus walkways and respect the artwork.

cards.entity_name: Louis D. Brandeis Burial Site Animal Crackers
cards.title: Leave Animal Crackers for Brandeis Luck
cards.subtitle: Louis D. Brandeis School of Law lore
cards.notes: If visiting the law school's Brandeis memorial area, learn about the animal-cracker good-luck ritual without leaving food or disturbing the site.
cards.short_summary: Law-student folklore links animal crackers at Justice Brandeis's burial site with luck.
cards.evidence_claim: A UofL News account of traditions says law students leave animal crackers at the burial site of Justice Louis D. Brandeis for luck.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as historical lore; do not leave food or items at a memorial without posted permission.

cards.title: Learn the U of L Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: University song tradition
cards.notes: Listen to the university's Alma Mater and follow along at an appropriate Cardinal gathering; Student Affairs lists it among UofL traditions.
cards.short_summary: The Alma Mater is formally identified by Student Affairs as a UofL tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UofL Student Affairs includes the Alma Mater in its Traditions section and links to the university's Alma Mater performance.
cards.access_notes: Listen or sing only where music and event etiquette permit.

cards.entity_name: UofL Fight Song and All Hail
cards.title: Join the Fight Song and All Hail
cards.subtitle: Cardinal athletic-song tradition
cards.notes: At a Cardinal event, listen for the Fight Song and All Hail and join in at the designated moment; Student Affairs lists both as traditions.
cards.short_summary: The Fight Song and All Hail are official entries in UofL's traditions listing.
cards.evidence_claim: UofL Student Affairs includes “Fight Song and All Hail” in its Traditions section.
cards.access_notes: Participate only during an event or performance where it is being led.

cards.title: Follow the Mr. and Ms. Cardinal Recognition
cards.subtitle: Student Affairs tradition
cards.notes: Look for announcements or historical displays recognizing Mr. and Ms. Cardinal; this named honor is maintained in Student Affairs' traditions section.
cards.short_summary: Mr. and Ms. Cardinal is a named Student Affairs tradition and recognition.
cards.evidence_claim: UofL Student Affairs lists Mr. and Ms. Cardinal among its traditions and provides a dedicated history link.
cards.access_notes: Check Student Affairs announcements for any current program details.

cards.title: Recognize Homecoming King and Queen
cards.subtitle: University Homecoming tradition
cards.notes: Follow Homecoming programming and recognize the named King and Queen tradition, which Student Affairs preserves with its other university-history materials.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming King and Queen is a formally listed UofL tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UofL Student Affairs includes Homecoming King and Queen in its Traditions section and provides a dedicated history link.
cards.access_notes: Consult official Homecoming announcements for current event timing and participation details.

cards.title: Attend or Follow the Legacy Awards
cards.subtitle: Student Affairs recognition tradition
cards.notes: Check Student Affairs communications for the next Legacy Awards program and learn which student leaders and contributors are being recognized that year.
cards.short_summary: Legacy Awards is one of the named traditions documented by UofL Student Affairs.
cards.evidence_claim: UofL Student Affairs lists Legacy Awards in its Traditions section and links to related awards materials.
cards.access_notes: Current schedule and eligibility are not stated on the cited traditions page.
